rationale: ⲉⲕⲱⲧ = Sahidic ⲕⲱⲧ 'to build, builder' with prosthetic vowel; standard Manichaean title for the Great Architect (μέγας Δημιουργός) of the cosmos.

Apostolic figure paralleling the cosmogonic First Man (ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ). Persecuted in the Church just as the First Man battled the primordial Darkness — typological pairing fundamental to Manichaean ecclesiology.
Lycopolitan feminine ordinal series ⲙⲁⲍ-N-ⲉ matching the abstract feminine ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲁⲅ. Pattern: ⲙⲁⲍ- (ordinal prefix) + numeral + -ⲉ (feminine ending).

Technical Manichaean grouping of the five primary divine emanations: (1) Father of Greatness, (2) Mother of Life with First Man and Five Sons, (3) Beloved of Lights / Great Builder / Living Spirit with Five Sons, (4) Third Ambassador with Pillar of Glory, (5) Jesus the Radiance with all his powers. Distinct from but overlapping with other Manichaean enumerations.
Lycopolitan form of ⲡϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ 'the four,' with assimilation of ϥ. Cf. ⲩⲧⲟⲉ in ⲙⲁⲍⲩⲧⲟⲉ 'fourth' on this page.
ⲧⲕⲉ- ('the other') + ⲧ̄ⲉ (= ϯⲟⲩ 'five') — used to distinguish the Five Sons of the Living Spirit from the Five Sons of the First Man.
ⲕⲱⲧ as nominal 'building, construction' — the entire fashioned cosmos as architectural artifact of the Great Builder. Standard Manichaean cosmological term.
Lycopolitan reflex of διώκειν / πῶτ — verb of pursuit and persecution. Used twice in line 2 in iterative-comparative construction 'persecute them as they persecuted...'.
Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said' — past tense of speech-introduction. Common in Kephalaia narrative frame: 'Once again the Illuminator ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ to his disciples...'
Greek πάλιν 'again' (ⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ with article-like ⲧ-) reinforced by Coptic ⲁⲛ 'again' — doubled adverb opening a new chapter's narrative frame.
